strings: Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road.

After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey.

Innkeeper Farley takes pride in his establishment's hospitality, operating under the motto of providing rest and relaxation for the tired and cold. Adventurers who mention their referral can take advantage of Farley's good graces, settling by the open fire to enjoy a warm meal, sturdy ale, and a much-needed respite before journeying further into Elwynn.
Where can I find the Lion's Pride Inn?
The Lion's Pride Inn is located south along the main road leading out of Northshire Valley, situated at the heart of the town of Goldshire. Travelers heading south cannot miss the welcoming tavern.
where is lions pride inn | how to get to lion's pride inn | find lions pride
Innkeeper Farley is the hospitable proprietor of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. A close friend of local contacts in Northshire, he welcomes weary adventurers with food, drink, and a warm hearth.
who is innkeeper farley | farley lion's pride
What is the purpose of Rest and Relaxation?

Rest and Relaxation directs novice adventurers leaving Northshire toward Goldshire's central hub, introducing them to the services, refreshments, and lodgings offered by Innkeeper Farley at the Lion's Pride Inn.
what is the purpose of this quest | why go to lion's pride inn

Mentioning your referral to Innkeeper Farley allows travelers to inquire about special discounted rates on the inn's fine food and drink while recovering from their travels.
discount at lions pride | do i get cheaper food farley
Why is rest important for traveling adventurers?

Adventuring across Elwynn is grueling and fraught with danger. Inns provide safe shelter from the wilderness, allowing travelers to warm their bones by the fire, recuperate, and replenish their supplies before taking on new tasks.
why do adventurers need rest | rest and relaxation lore
What is the motto of the Lion's Pride Inn?
According to Innkeeper Farley, the inn's motto is 'Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold.' He strives to ensure every weary guest finds comfort and hospitality by his hearth.
what is lions pride inn motto | lions pride slogan

The Lion's Pride Inn serves as the primary haven and social hub for Alliance travelers venturing out into Elwynn Forest.
Fresh recruits departing Northshire Valley naturally follow the southern road toward Goldshire, where Innkeeper Farley offers familiar hospitality close to Stormwind.

Dolanaar Delivery is an errand entrusted to young night elves leaving the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen for the wider reaches of Teldrassil. Porthannius, detained by affairs with the local druids, tasks travelers with carrying a parcel of herbs south to Innkeeper Keldamyr. The simple journey marks an initiate's transition into the bustling hub of Dolanaar.

Before new adventurers depart the training grounds of Shadowglen, Porthannius seeks someone heading down the road toward the rest of Teldrassil. Entangled in pressing business with the druids tending the glade, he cannot step away to run routine errands himself. Instead, he places a bundle of freshly harvested herbs into the hands of an aspiring hero to ensure vital supplies make it south along the forest path.

Following the southern road out of the secluded vale leads travelers to Dolanaar, one of the foremost night elf settlements upon the great boughs of Teldrassil. There, Innkeeper Keldamyr oversees hospitality, rest, and supplies for wanderers, sentinels, and druids alike. Receiving the herbs on Porthannius's behalf, Keldamyr uses the occasion to urge young adventurers to rest their minds and spirits before confronting the growing corruption across the world tree.

Porthannius is a night elf residing in Shadowglen, Teldrassil's starting glade. While working closely alongside the local druids, he enlists travelers leaving the glade to ferry supplies southward on his behalf.
porthannius | who gives dolanaar delivery | quest giver porthannius

Porthannius has urgent, unfinished business with the druids of Shadowglen. Because his duties keep him occupied within the sheltered vale, he must rely on passing adventurers to make the journey south.

The delivery illustrates how vital raw herbs from Shadowglen's verdant soils are to the healers, cooks, and caretakers of Dolanaar.
Taking this task marks a night elf's departure from the protected cradle of Aldrassil out into the broader responsibilities of safeguarding Teldrassil.

Porthannius has prepared a vital bundle of fresh herbs gathered in Shadowglen that Innkeeper Keldamyr is awaiting down in Dolanaar. However, urgent duties keep Porthannius occupied with the local druids, preventing him from making the journey down the road himself. To ensure the innkeeper receives these necessary supplies without delay, he relies on a passing traveler heading out into Teldrassil.

Supplies to Tannok is an errand entrusted to fledgling adventurers departing Coldridge Valley through the dangerous mountain pass into greater Dun Morogh. The gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket sends a crate of needed provisions to Tannok Frosthammer at the Thunderbrew Distillery inn in Kharanos, bypassing the trogg-infested trails that have severed routine trade.

Coldridge Valley is traditionally the proving ground and sanctuary for young Ironforge dwarves and exiled Gnomeregan survivors, but recent events have strained its connection to the rest of Dun Morogh. Trogg incursions have overrun Coldridge Pass, leaving the mountain defile perilous to cross. Mountaineers are spread thin guarding settlements and defensive perimeters, delaying scheduled supply escorts for days on end.

Hands Springsprocket, a gnome waiting by the mouth of Coldridge Pass, found himself saddled with a crate of vital inn supplies meant for Kharanos without any safe way to deliver it personally. Recognizing that hearty adventurers are already preparing to brave the perilous pass, he enlists outward-bound travelers to carry the cargo to Tannok Frosthammer, the assistant at the bustling Thunderbrew inn.

Reaching Kharanos marks an adventurer's entry into the broader world of Dun Morogh. Tannok Frosthammer eagerly receives the delivery, noting that word from Anvilmar has been scarce ever since the troggs disrupted travel through the pass. Delivering the goods restores a fragile line of communication and trade between the two isolated dwarf communities.

Hands Springsprocket is an enterprising gnome stationed by the mouth of Coldridge Pass in Coldridge Valley. Unable to traverse the dangerous mountain pass alone, he relies on capable travelers to transport goods to Kharanos.
hands springsprocket | quest giver | who gives supplies to tannok

tannok | tannok frosthammer | kharanos innkeeper assistant

The pass connecting Coldridge Valley to Kharanos has been overrun by hostile troggs. Hands is not equipped to fight his way through alone, and official Mountaineer escorts are heavily delayed.

what is in the crate | crate of inn supplies

Troggs emerging from subterranean tunnels have flooded Coldridge Pass. Their aggressive presence has severed easy foot travel and regular dispatches between Coldridge Valley and the rest of Dun Morogh.

Restoring trade between isolated outposts keeps Ironforge's inland supply lines moving despite wild trogg incursions.
Carrying supplies from Anvilmar to Kharanos marks your rite of passage out of the sheltered valley and into service to the broader kingdom of Ironforge.
Helping Hands Springsprocket demonstrates the reliable cooperation between Gnomeregan exiles and their dwarven hosts in Dun Morogh.
Why does Hands Springsprocket want the supplies delivered to Kharanos?

Hands Springsprocket promised vital provisions to Tannok Frosthammer, the assistant at the Kharanos inn, but trogg attacks have shut down travel through the pass out of Coldridge Valley. With regular shipments stranded and Mountaineer escorts days away, Tannok is left waiting and worrying with dwindling supplies. Hands wants to honor his delivery and ensure the bustling Thunderbrew Distillery and inn stay stocked for road-weary travelers.
why send supplies to tannok | hands springsprocket motive | why deliver crate of inn supplies

A Peon's Burden is an introductory delivery task given by Ukor, an anxious orc laborer stranded along the trail outside the Valley of Trials. After attempting to deliver provisions to new recruits who turned out not to need them, Ukor entrusts travelers with returning the heavy load safely to Razor Hill.

Ukor is an earnest peon who set out from Razor Hill with good intentions, hauling a heavy pack of provisions toward the Valley of Trials. Believing the fresh recruits training in the red canyon were in dire need of rations, he braved the road only to be turned away. The taskmasters overseeing the trials deliberately keep supplies lean—as Innkeeper Grosk later notes, surviving on meager sustenance is seen as a way to forge discipline and endurance in young Horde warriors.

Though he managed to make it to the pass, Ukor finds himself terrified of retracing his steps across the sun-baked soil of Durotar. The crags along the trail teem with aggressive scorpids, venomous spiders, and prowling boars. Lacking weapons, armor, or the fighting spirit expected of orcish grunts, the frightened laborer waits along the path, pleading for any passing adventurer departing the proving grounds to shoulder his burden and return it to the inn.

Ukor is an orc peon stationed along the road leading out of the Valley of Trials. Well-meaning but timid, he ventured out to deliver provisions from Razor Hill before realizing he was too terrified of local wildlife to make the return journey on his own.
ukor | who is the peon on the road | peon near valley of trials
Why didn't the trainers in the Valley of Trials want the food?

The overseers in the Valley of Trials believe in rigorous discipline for fledgling recruits. As Innkeeper Grosk humorously points out, the instructors prefer to keep the trainees hungry to test their mettle and build their spirit, rendering Ukor's charitable shipment unwelcome.
why refuse food | why did ukor carry food | innkeeper grosk starvation
Where does this delivery need to go?
The burden must be carried north along Durotar's main thoroughfare to Razor Hill, where it is handed over to Innkeeper Grosk inside the settlement's tavern.
where is razor hill | who do i give the food to | where to deliver ukor's burden
What makes the journey dangerous for a peon?

Durotar's rocky wastes are filled with territorial scorpids, venomous crawler spiders, and wild boars. While seasoned recruits can handle such vermin, an unarmored and untrained laborer like Ukor stands little chance if set upon.
why is ukor scared | durotar road dangers
What is the role of peons in the Horde?

Peons occupy the lowest rung of orcish society, handling menial labor such as hauling supplies, chopping timber, and erecting fortifications. While grunts and champions receive praise and glory, peons are often overlooked despite keeping settlements fed and maintained.
orc peons lore | peon status | what are peons

Innkeeper Grosk runs the inn in Razor Hill. He manages the town's lodgings and supplies, offering food, drink, and hearth to traveling warriors and reminding recruits that resting is vital before taking on the wider world.
innkeeper grosk | grosk razor hill | razor hill innkeeper

This trek serves as a transition out of the proving grounds, introducing travelers to Razor Hill, the central hub for Horde defense and logistics in southern Durotar.

Orcish culture prizes physical might and courage, leaving peons like Ukor at the very bottom of the social hierarchy; taking on his errand shows how even humble labor keeps the fledgling nation of Durotar functioning.
Why does Ukor want the food delivered back to Razor Hill?

Ukor genuinely meant well when he hauled supplies out from Razor Hill, hoping to aid the young recruits training under the harsh sun of the Valley of Trials. Finding that the trainers turned the rations away, he cannot simply abandon the supplies or let them spoil on the road. The food belongs back on the shelves of Innkeeper Grosk's pantry, but after barely surviving the trek past the region's scorpids and spiders, Ukor is terrified of making the perilous return trip alone.
why return the food | ukor motive | why give food to grosk
Why does Ukor ask you to carry the burden instead of doing it himself?

Ukor is an ordinary peon, unaccustomed to violence and unarmed against the wilderness. While he managed to brave the scorpions and spiders on the road leading out from Razor Hill, the sheer terror of facing those savage predators again has frozen him in place. Spotting you emerging victorious from the Valley of Trials, he sees a capable hero who fears nothing, hoping you will gladly carry the burden on your way to Razor Hill.

In Defense of the King's Lands

In Defense of the King's Lands culminates with a direct strike against the leadership of the trogg incursion in Loch Modan. Dwarven scouts trace the violent infestation to Chieftain Grawmug and his brute bodyguards deep within Stonesplinter Valley. Captain Rugelfuss tasks bold Alliance adventurers with slaying the chieftain to shatter trogg morale and reclaim the realm's southern borders.

The persistent trogg menace across southern Loch Modan has proven to be more than random subterranean crawling. Captain Rugelfuss's scouts discovered that the Stonesplinter troggs are operating under the crude direction of a chieftain named Grawmug. Unlike typical scattered marauders, this pack moves with concerted aggression, threatening to overrun the King's Lands if left unchecked. By taking the fight into their lair and executing Grawmug alongside his personal bruisers, the Dwarven defenders hope to break the pack's cohesion and stem the tide.

Grawmug makes his stand within a shadowy cavern tucked into the southeastern cliffs of Stonesplinter Valley. Surrounded by his most trusted brutes, Gnasher and Brawler, the chieftain presents a dangerous challenge for lone soldiers. Striking down this inner circle forces the remaining troggs into disarray, buying the beleaguered Mountaineers the opportunity they desperately need to fortify the roads and drive the beasts back into the dark depths.

Grawmug is the vicious trogg chieftain rallying the Stonesplinter troggs in southern Loch Modan. Dwarven scouts identified him as the mastermind behind the organized assaults troubling the valley, keeping two formidable bodyguards, Gnasher and Brawler, at his side at all times.
grawmug lore | who is the trogg leader | chieftain grawmug
Where are Grawmug and his guards located?
Grawmug, Gnasher, and Brawler are entrenched inside a cave on the southeastern edge of Stonesplinter Valley in Loch Modan. They dwell deep in the cavern recesses together.
grawmug location | where is grawmug | where to find grawmug

Captain Rugelfuss is the dwarven officer stationed at the Southern Guard Tower in Loch Modan. He oversees the defensive campaigns against the encroaching trogg incursions and issues orders to protect the territorial integrity of the King's Lands.

Why must Grawmug's guards be slain as well?

Gnasher and Brawler are Grawmug's personal enforcers who never leave his flank. To eliminate the chieftain and definitively break the leadership of the trogg offensive, both heavy protectors must be defeated alongside their leader.
why kill gnasher and brawler | gnasher and brawler | grawmug bodyguards
What happens after Grawmug is eliminated?

Slaying Grawmug brings vital relief to Loch Modan. Without their chieftain to coordinate their raids, the Stonesplinter troggs lose organization, allowing the local dwarven militia to stand a fighting chance at holding the borders and pushing the beasts underground.

Why are troggs invading Loch Modan?

Troggs have long festered deep within subterranean chambers beneath Khaz Modan. Excavations and unsealed caverns have allowed them to boil to the surface, where they aggressively displace settlements and attack travelers on the King's roads.
why are troggs here | trogg invasion loch modan | stonesplinter trogg origin

Defending Loch Modan preserves the vital overland connection between Ironforge and the eastern frontiers, keeping supply lines secure for all Alliance forces.
For dwarves, repelling troggs from Khaz Modan's ancient soil is a matter of homeland defense and honor, ensuring the mountain holds remain unblemished by subterranean scourges.
Why does Captain Rugelfuss want Grawmug killed?

Captain Rugelfuss sees Grawmug as the mastermind driving the trogg incursions threatening Loch Modan. The dwarven garrisons have been struggling to hold back the subterranean swarms, and Rugelfuss believes that decapitating their leadership—specifically eliminating Grawmug alongside his elite bodyguards—will break their momentum and give the dwarves a fighting chance to drive them back underground.

Easy Strider Living is a local culinary task offered by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine. She is eager to share her prized recipe for strider stew, provided an adventurer is willing to hunt down the fierce foreststriders wandering Darkshore and retrieve their meat.

Auberdine might be a quiet port village, but survival along the coast requires making good use of the local wildlife. Alanndarian Nightsong has developed a secret recipe for hearty strider stew, a savory dish made from the tall, fleet-footed foreststriders that stalk the shadowy woods of Darkshore. Rather than simply handing out culinary secrets, she asks aspiring cooks and hunters to venture out and cull the birds themselves.

Foreststriders are swift, sharp-beaked avian predators that roam the mist-shrouded woodlands and beaches north and south of Auberdine. While they can be temperamental and aggressive when provoked, their succulent meat makes an excellent base for a rich stew. Bringing back fresh meat satisfies Alanndarian's hungry pot and earns the hunter her cherished recipe.

Alanndarian Nightsong is a night elf resident of Auberdine in Darkshore. Known for her simmering pot of strider stew, she offers to teach her culinary craft to travelers who prove their hunting prowess.

This task is essential for culinarians traveling through Darkshore, rewarding the recipe to prepare nourishing Strider Stew from local wildlife.
Living harmoniously in Kalimdor often involves living off the land, and hearty strider stews have become a coastal staple for night elves in Auberdine.

The succulent meat is the core ingredient in Alanndarian's savory strider stew. Bringing her five cuts fills her empty kettle and proves to her that you have earned the right to learn her secret wilderness recipe.

The Stolen Journal is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh where Grelin Whitebeard tasks adventurers with entering the troll cave in Coldridge Valley to reclaim his stolen notebook. To recover it, you must defeat the formidable troll leader Grik'nir the Cold. Reclaiming the journal allows Grelin to finalize his appraisal of the troll threat within Coldridge Valley.

Grelin Whitebeard has been observing the Frostmane trolls encroaching on Coldridge Valley, keeping detailed notes on their habits and sudden aggression. During the unrest, an unusually imposing troll made off with his personal journal and retreated into the depths of their den. For Grelin, the loss is not merely sentimental; the notebook contains the bulk of his reconnaissance, leaving his official assessment stalled until it is recovered from the cavern.

The brute responsible for taking the journal is Grik'nir the Cold, a powerful Frostmane troll marked with distinctive body and facial paint who holds court in the heart of the valley's troll cave. Slaying Grik'nir breaks the immediate local leadership of the cave's trolls and secures Grelin's journal. With the leader dispatched, Grelin feels confident enough to report that the valley's troll situation is manageable, sending his finished findings on to his brother Senir.
The journal was taken by Grik'nir the Cold, a large Frostmane troll distinguished by strange markings on his skin and face who lurks deep within the troll cave.

Grelin is compiling an official report on the Frostmane threat in Coldridge Valley for his brother Senir. Without his journal, he cannot complete his notes or assess the safety of the valley, leaving local leaders without crucial intelligence on troll activity.

Grelin is an observer rather than a frontline fighter, and the journal was carried deep into the troll cave of Coldridge Valley by a formidable troll brute. Having already witnessed your success fighting back the trolls in the valley, he turns to you to delve into the cave and handle the danger.

Missing In Action is an Alliance escort mission in the Redridge Mountains to rescue Corporal Keeshan from Blackrock orc captivity. After his regiment was wiped out in the hills, Keeshan was knocked unconscious and dragged into a cave fortress. Guiding the wounded soldier safely back to Lakeshire helps the local garrison confirm the grim fate of their missing men.

The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as Blackrock orcs descend from the northern peaks. Patrols sent out by the town guard frequently run into ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's unit suffered the worst of it. Outnumbered and overwhelmed, most of the soldiers in his regiment were cut down on the spot. Keeshan survived only because a crushing blow knocked him cold before he could be executed, allowing the orcs to drag him back to their cave as a prisoner.

Battered, concussed, and held deep within enemy territory, Keeshan could not make the trek back down the mountain alone. Escorting him down to the safety of Lakeshire takes him past swarming orc warbands that occupy the ridgelines. Reaching Lakeshire alive brings sorely needed relief to Marshal Marris, who has been trying to piece together what happened to the missing regiment while bracing Lakeshire for further attacks.

Corporal Keeshan is an Alliance infantryman stationed in the Redridge Mountains. During a patrol in the rocky hills, his regiment was overwhelmed by Blackrock orcs, leaving him the sole known survivor before he was dragged away into captivity.
corporal keeshan | who is keeshan | keeshan lore
He is held captive deep inside an orc-infested cave in the northern hills of Redridge, surrounded by hostile Blackrock warriors.

Having suffered a severe blow to the head during the skirmish, he is badly wounded, disoriented, and in need of an escort. Goretusk Liver Pie is a culinary errand undertaken for Salma Saldean at the Saldean Farm in Westfall. With the breadbasket of the kingdom ravaged by bandits, local homesteaders rely on hunting the aggressive local boars to put a hearty meal on the table. Assisting Salma provides a rare taste of comfort and home-cooked hospitality in an otherwise bleak frontier.

Westfall was once the fertile breadbasket of Stormwind, but recent years have brought hard times. With neglected infrastructure, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields, everyday life has become a grind for the few remaining settlers. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works tirelessly to maintain a sense of hearth and home despite the encroaching dangers. Preparing a traditional meat pie represents one of the few modest luxuries available to homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life.

Translate Abercrombie's Note is an Alliance quest in Darkshire that tasks an adventurer with carrying an indecipherable letter to the town's resident scholar. Lord Ello Ebonlocke cannot make sense of the hermit's missive, relying instead on Sirra Von'Indi's knowledge of obscure scripts. It marks the moment Darkshire's leadership begins to look closely at the hermit's strange letter.

When Abercrombie dispatches a sealed letter to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, the town leader expects an eccentric plea or bitter ramblings from the cemetery hermit. Instead, the parchment is inscribed in strange, cryptic writing that defies standard Common script. Lacking the scholarly training to decipher ancient or esoteric languages, Mayor Ebonlocke refuses to dismiss the letter out of hand, knowing that even mad hermits can pose a hazard in Duskwood.

To crack the cipher, Ebonlocke directs travelers across the square to Sirra Von'Indi. Sirra is Darkshire's scholar of esoteric lore, well-versed in ancient arts and forgotten tongues. Though Sirra scoffs at Abercrombie's sanity—quipping that anyone dwelling beside a haunted graveyard must have rotted brains—he takes the parchment seriously enough to begin the painstaking process of transcription.

The call directs adventurers into Tinkertown to prepare for a perilous venture into the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan.

Word travels far even in troubled times. When Klockmort Spannerspan found himself in need of bold allies for a mission into Gnomeregan, he reached out across the sea to his night elf acquaintance, Mathiel. Mathiel, bound to his own post, cannot journey to the mountain kingdom himself, but he refuses to leave his friend's plea unanswered. Instead, he appeals to capable Alliance adventurers visiting him on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus to make the trek to Dun Morogh on his behalf.

Klockmort Spannerspan operates out of Tinkertown, the bustling refugee district of Ironforge where displaced gnomes have gathered since the catastrophic fall of their underground city. Amid the whir of gears and clouds of steam, Klockmort is formulating plans to retrieve vital machinery left behind in Gnomeregan's contaminated corridors. Taking Mathiel's referral leads adventurers directly to Klockmort's workshop, enlisting them in his reclamation efforts.

Gnogaine is an Alliance quest offered by Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. In an eccentric attempt to synthesize a cure for the leper gnomes—or perhaps concoct an extraordinarily potent beverage—Ozzie tasks adventurers with venturing toward Gnomeregan to gather radioactive fallout from glowing troggs.

Ever since the fall of Gnomeregan, refugees like Gnoarn have fixated entirely on exterminating the trogg invaders and reversing the radioactive affliction that mutated their brethren. In contrast, Ozzie Togglevolt and his partner Razzle Sprysprocket take a somewhat less orthodox approach from their workshop in Kharanos. While purporting to pursue a cure for the leper gnomes, Ozzie openly admits their experimental formula might just as easily end up being a recipe for remarkably strong rum.

To refine their concoction, the inventors require raw toxic residue directly from the epicenter of the catastrophe. Equipping adventurers with a leaden collection phial, Ozzie sends them toward the breached tunnels of Gnomeregan. There, roving irradiated invaders and pillagers—troggs saturated with leaking waste—glow with the sickening green energy needed to charge the flask.

Upon securing a full phial of green glow, Ozzie wastes no time preparing a live trial. Beyond hoping to restore sanity and health to a captured leper gnome, the tinkerer harbors personal aspirations for the brew, believing the fallout mixture might also miraculously cure his baldness.
The quest is given by Ozzie Togglevolt, a gnome tinkerer stationed in Kharanos within Dun Morogh.

What are the irradiated troggs in Gnomeregan?
